questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The production possibility curve for an economy producing capital goods and consumer goods is represented by the line PQ. P capital goods T R O S Q consumer goods What is the opportunity cost of producing OS of consumer goods?

options.A: OR of capital goods
options.B: PR of capital goods
options.C: SQ of consumer goods
options.D: SQ of consumer goods + PR of capital goods

questions.questionText: In the diagram XY is an economy’s production possibility curve. X financial services O Y Z manufactured goods What could cause the curve to shift to XZ?

options.A: a fall in productivity in manufacturing
options.B: a fall in the price of manufactured goods
options.C: a higher demand for manufactured goods
options.D: an improvement in manufacturing technology

questions.questionText: Very heavy rain often causes houses to flood. The government protects the area with flood defence schemes while households buy sandbags to protect their houses. How would an economist classify these items? flood defence sandbags schemes

options.A: merit goods private goods
options.B: merit goods public goods
options.C: public goods private goods
options.D: public goods public goods

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for air travel in Asia. price D D O quantity If air travel is a normal good, what could have caused the shift in the demand curve from D to D ?

options.A: a fall in employment in Asia
options.B: a fall in the price of aviation fuel
options.C: an increase in road congestion
options.D: an increase in the price of train travel

questions.questionText: What will not cause a shift in the market supply curve of a commodity?

options.A: a change in technology
options.B: a rise in the price of a factor input
options.C: a rise in the price of the commodity
options.D: the introduction of a specific tax on the commodity

questions.questionText: A government imposes a tax on a good. The equilibrium price rises by the same amount as the tax. What can be concluded about the price elasticity of demand for the good?

options.A: It is perfectly elastic.
options.B: It is perfectly inelastic.
options.C: It is unitary.
options.D: Nothing can be determined about price elasticity of demand.

questions.questionText: What can be concluded about a product which has an income elasticity of demand (YED) of –1.5 and a cross-elasticity of demand (XED) of +1.2 with another product? YED figure XED figure

options.A: The product is an inferior good. The other product is a complement.
options.B: The product is an inferior good. The other product is a substitute.
options.C: The product is a normal good. The other product is a complement.
options.D: The product is a normal good. The other product is a substitute.

questions.questionText: A product has a low price elasticity of supply. What might explain this?

options.A: The product has a low opportunity cost.
options.B: The product has a perishable nature.
options.C: The product is classed as an inferior good.
options.D: The product is considered to be a necessity.

questions.questionText: A firm is producing 100 units at price $10. The price elasticity of supply is 0.5, and price is raised to $12. What is the new level of output?

The diagram shows the market for coffee in a small coffee-producing country. The domestic supply of coffee is represented by S . The supply curve of imports was initially Sm . A bad d 1 harvest that affects only other coffee-producing countries shifts the supply curve of imports to Sm . S d Sm price Sm D O T V W quantity How will consumption and imports be affected by the supply change?

options.A: Consumption falls by VW and imports fall to OT.
options.B: Consumption falls by VW and imports fall to zero.
options.C: Consumption is unchanged and imports fall to OT.
options.D: Consumption is unchanged and imports fall to zero.

questions.questionText: When demand for a good falls, its price falls. What is the function of the price fall?

options.A: to eliminate shortages
options.B: to reduce consumer surplus
options.C: to send a signal to producers
options.D: to stimulate a further fall in demand

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for computers in Pakistan. W S price Y X D O Z quantity What can be concluded about the value of consumer surplus?

options.A: It is less than producer revenue.
options.B: It is less than producer surplus.
options.C: It is more than producer revenue.
options.D: It is more than producer surplus.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves of a good. S price J D O quantity The government sets a maximum price of OJ for the good. How will this affect the consumers and producers of the good? effect on consumers effect on producers

options.A: All consumers will gain. Producers will lose.
options.B: All consumers will gain. Producers will gain.
options.C: Some consumers will gain and some will lose. Producers will gain.
options.D: Some consumers will gain and some will lose. Producers will lose.

questions.questionText: A simple income tax system would be one in which income under $10000 is not taxed. Above $10000 an income tax rate of 30% is applied to all additional income. What is correct for people earning more than $10000? average rate of tax marginal rate of tax

options.A: increases as incomes increase increases as incomes increase
options.B: increases as incomes increase remains constant as incomes increase
options.C: remains constant as incomes increase increases as incomes increase
options.D: remains constant as incomes increase remains constant as incomes increase

questions.questionText: The diagram shows possible demand and supply curves for places in colleges in a country. The initial equilibrium position is X. To increase the number of students in colleges, a government subsidises the colleges and also gives a grant of money to the students. What would be the new equilibrium position? D B S A price X C S D D O college places
Which term is given to an income received by an individual for which there is no corresponding contribution to output?

options.A: profit
options.B: revenue
options.C: salary
options.D: transfer payment

questions.questionText: A government’s budget deficit was reduced. What might have caused this?

options.A: a decrease in the revenue from vehicle tax
options.B: an increase in the rate of subsidy given to libraries
options.C: a purchase of two warships for the national defence
options.D: a sale of a publicly owned energy company to the private sector

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate supply curves and aggregate demand curves for an economy. SRAS SRAS price X level Y AD AD O real output What is most likely to cause the equilibrium position to move from X to Y?

options.A: a decrease in corporation tax and a decrease in labour productivity
options.B: a decrease in interest rates and a decrease in electricity prices
options.C: an increase in interest rates and an increase in raw material costs
options.D: an increase in marginal tax rates and a decrease in labour productivity

questions.questionText: The table shows the share of a worker’s income spent on three classes of good and the percentage change in the prices of the goods over a year. share of income change in spent on goods prices of goods clothing 25% +25% food 50% +50% fuel 25% –25% Over the same period the worker’s money income rises by 25%. What happens to the worker’s real income?

options.A: It falls by 25%.
options.B: It falls by 50%.
options.C: It rises by 25%.
options.D: It is unchanged.

questions.questionText: Over a period of a year, the annual rate of inflation becomes negative. Which statement must be correct?

options.A: The cost of living has fallen.
options.B: The purchasing power of money has fallen.
options.C: The standard of living has increased.
options.D: There has been an increase in the Consumer Price Index.

questions.questionText: What would cause an immediate increase in the deficit in a country’s balance of payments on the current account?

options.A: a rise in government expenditure on education
options.B: a rise in the cost of imported raw materials used in domestic production
options.C: a rise in the foreign ownership of domestic companies
options.D: a rise in the total wages earned by nationals working abroad

questions.questionText: The table shows the Canadian current account of the balance of payments in 2005 and 2006. The change in which item contributed the most to the move from surplus to deficit in the Canadian current account balance between 2005 and 2006? 2005 2006 ($m) ($m)

options.A: balance of trade in goods 62372 –4568
options.B: balance of trade in services 12055 –22663
options.C: investment income balance –22917 –14145
options.D: transfers balance –1498 –2148 total 25902 –43523

questions.questionText: A depreciation of the exchange rate of the UK pound (£) against the US dollar ($) from £1:$1.50 to £1:$1.00 must mean that

options.A: dollars will become more expensive in terms of pounds.
options.B: the pound will be undervalued.
options.C: UK imports from the US will become cheaper.
options.D: US imports from the UK will become more expensive.

questions.questionText: A country has no controls on transactions in foreign exchange and allows its exchange rate to float freely. What will always be zero?

options.A: net inward investment
options.B: the country’s foreign exchange reserves
options.C: the current account balance of payments position
options.D: the overall balance of payments position

questions.questionText: The table gives the terms of trade index for Brunei Darussalam for the period 2009 to 2012. 2009 2010 2011 2012 terms of trade index 100.0 107.2 124.9 134.5 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Export prices were 34.5% higher in 2012 than in 2009.
options.B: Import prices were 34.5% lower in 2012 than in 2009.
options.C: The ratio of export to import prices was 34.5% higher in 2012 than in 2009.
options.D: The terms of trade increased by 34.5% during 2012.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s production possibility curve, PPC, and trading possibility curve, TPC. food TPC PPC O clothing Why is the diagram not able to demonstrate the benefits of international trade?

options.A: It assumes there are no transport costs and no barriers to trade.
options.B: It deals with only two products.
options.C: The curves are drawn as straight lines.
options.D: The position of the curves does not support the existence of benefits.

questions.questionText: Which government policy will increase aggregate demand?

options.A: raising indirect taxation
options.B: reducing the budget surplus
options.C: removing domestic subsidies
options.D: removing import quotas

questions.questionText: What would be the best policy for a country to reduce a balance of payments deficit?

options.A: an increase in interest rates
options.B: an increase in the exchange rate
options.C: a reduction in direct taxes
options.D: a reduction in subsidies to domestic industry

questions.questionText: Country X is an open economy with a fixed exchange rate. Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies would be most effective in reversing a deflation? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: lower direct taxes devaluation
options.B: lower direct taxes revaluation
options.C: lower indirect taxes devaluation
